key_insight: A logarithmic correction with exponent 1/3 enables a constant, positive energy cascade in 2D quantum-fluid wave turbulence where the naive power law predicts thermal equilibrium.
engineering_relevance: The corrected spectrum can improve interpretation of 2D Bose-gas measurements and guide spectral diagnostics in quantum-fluid simulations.
method: Asymptotically expand the wave-kinetic collision integral to derive the logarithmic correction.
Set the logarithmic cutoff by the small-scale dissipation scale.
Regularize the marginal infrared divergence at the forcing scale to estimate the spectral prefactor.
evidence_signal: Gross–Pitaevskii and wave-kinetic simulations support the predicted spectral shape, while finite-range steepening offers a possible explanation for experimental spectra.
watch_item: The prefactor estimate assumes widely separated forcing and dissipation scales, so finite spectral ranges require caution.
paper_title: Energy cascade spectrum in wave turbulence of a two-dimensional quantum fluid
